facts.name: Spotted Bee Balm
facts.color: Spotted yellow flowers in pink-lavender bracts
facts.moisture: Dry to average, sandy, well drained
facts.notes: An odd and lovely bee balm: tiers of purple-spotted yellow flowers ringed by pink and lavender bracts, stacked up the stem. A magnet for native bees and wasps, more drought tolerant than other bee balms, and its smell keeps deer and rabbits away. Often short-lived, but it reseeds in open, sandy soil.

sources.title: MSU Native Plants: Horsemint (Spotted bee balm)
sources.note: Michigan native in MSU's native plant trials; tolerates extremely dry soil; blooms through August; 1 to 3 ft.
